newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks end up on gains by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks end up on gains by blue chips.

text.p: Dhaka stocks, propelled by renewed commitments by investors, closed higher ahead of weekend, but the market was unlikely to maintain its upward trend next week because of pressure from banks on repayment of loans, brokers said.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange benchmark index rose 12.72 points or 1.14 percent at 1,123.18 on a turnover of 53.9 million taka. Gainers led losers by 90 to 38.

"Blue-chips like leasing company IDLC, Singer Bangladesh, Apex Foods, Monno Ceramic and Delta Life Insurance benefited most as the institutional investors made fresh commitments," said broker Imtiyaz Husain.
Brokers said forecasts of brighter company prospect by IDLC, Singer Bangladesh and Delta Life Insurance in their recent annual meetings attracted investors pushing their share prices up.
Singer Bangladesh was the top on the gainers list that rose 142 taka to 6,075. Apex Foods rose 81 to 2,200.

Monno Ceramic was one of the attractive scrips after the news that the company, that had been shut since Sunday, would resume production soon following a settlemnt of a labour dispute. Its share gained 72 taka to 802.

Delta Life Insurance rallied for a third day after the company announced higher profits on Tuesday gaining 39.49 taka to 1,202.11. Beximco Pharmaceuticals, having a strong financial base, was the volume leader for a straight second day with 32,650 shares trading at 145.52 taka each, up 3.98.
